regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters on the headline — but IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, and core sector decelerated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) while manufacturing slips to 52.8; goods-economy momentum is fading even as the survey headline holds. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirms investment demand is real, but the divergence between services buoyancy and goods deceleration is the fault line — if services PMI softens even 2 points, the composite drops below the level that justifies current equity multiples.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY masks a dangerous internal split: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) is accelerating while core CPI sits at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile). The inversion here is critical — low core gives RBI political cover to hold, but fuel at this level feeds into transport costs, which feed into food logistics, which feeds back into CFPI food at 5.52% YoY within two quarters. WPI at 9.92% YoY is the leading indicator: producer prices are running hot, and the pass-through to CPI core is a matter of timing, not probability.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) only partially captures. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding markets are being tapped to bridge the gap — exactly the dynamic that preceded IL&FS. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% with repo at 5.25% p.a. was FY14; within 12 months, external shocks forced emergency tightening. The setup rhymes. Watch for RBI risk-weight circulars on unsecured and NBFC lending as the macro-prudential lever of first resort.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is shifting: with CPI at 4.45% YoY and RBI's own inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% YoY, the real repo rate is barely positive at 80bps. A rate cut from here — which the market is partially pricing — would compress real rates to near zero precisely as fuel inflation is at a 95th-percentile print. The second-order effect: a premature cut signals INR weakness to FII desks already watching US 10Y at 5.28% yield, accelerating outflows and forcing RBI to intervene in FX — spending reserves to defend a rate decision that should not have been made.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY is the strongest signal in today's data — and it is corroborated by capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity from 75.6%, now at the 74th percentile. Credit to industry at 20.0% YoY and credit to services at 22.9% YoY confirm that capex financing is broad-based, not concentrated. The inversion: core sector growth slowing to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% means the physical infrastructure inputs (steel, cement, electricity) are not accelerating at the same pace as the capital goods order book — either there is a lag, or some of the IIP capex number is inventory restocking rather than new capacity creation.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong print, but the prior month was ₹1,74,116 cr / month — a jump of this magnitude in a single month demands decomposition before celebration. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY, two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY, and commercial vehicles at 16.88% YoY suggest demand is broad-based across income segments, which is the genuine signal. But GST volatility of this scale often reflects advance filings, festive season front-loading, or formalization reclassification — not a step-change in underlying demand. Triangulate against e-way bill volumes before treating this as a consumption breakout.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (latest, down from 82.5% prior) remains elevated at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.6% prior) signals wholesale funding pressure mounting.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either deposit acceleration or RBI easing. Last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest, up from 75.6% prior) — at 74th percentile of 10-year range — indicates headroom for capex without overcapacity risk. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (latest, down from 6% prior) is moderating but remains positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (latest, up from 6.5% prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.2% prior) confirm broad-based capex financing.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Domestic equipment manufacturers and project-linked contractors will see order book expansion. Infrastructure bonds and PSU capex plays (NTPC, Power Grid, NHAI) are attractive on 6-12 month horizon. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex cycle crowds out consumption.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates most aggressively when CU moves from 75% to 82%. This cycle has 500-700 bps of upside.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Ticket Size Rising","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (latest, up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 92nd percentile of 10-year range. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (latest, up from 99.06 mn prior) at 82nd percentile. SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 93rd percentile. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 85.76 ₹ lakh cr prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 86th percentile. DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month prior) — at 100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months.","implication":"SIP AUM growing 2.3% month-on-month while SIP accounts growing 1.1% signals average ticket size rising — affluent money entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour. Rotate from small-cap to large-cap and quality mid-caps. Domestic institutional support (DII at all-time high) provides downside cushion; use any 3-5% correction to add to quality names. Avoid micro-cap and speculative segments.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile preceded the 2021 bull run and the 2023-24 rally. When SIP AUM growth outpaces account growth by >100 bps, it signals wealth concentration and late-cycle positioning.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY prior) — at 95th percentile of 10-year range and tagged strong-negative signal. WPI at 9.92% YoY (latest, up from 9.78% YoY prior) — at 67th percentile. Brent crude at 100.47 $/bbl (latest, flat) but recent trend shows 102.4 $/bbl 6 months ago; volatility elevated. Natural gas at 3.077 $/MMBtu (latest, flat) — at 19th percentile but rising from 2.94 $/MMBtu lows. India's fuel import bill exposed to further crude spikes.","implication":"RBI will struggle to cut rates if fuel inflation stays > 20% YoY; expect inflation forecast revisions upward in next policy. Monitor geopolitical risk (Middle East, Russia) — a 10% crude spike would push CPI to 5%+, forcing RBI to hold or hike.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile last occurred in 2022 (pre-RBI tightening cycle). Sustained fuel inflation > 20% YoY has historically preceded 100-150 bps of rate hikes.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Bias Resurfaces; Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (latest, up from 3.63% p.a. prior) — rising 2 in a row and at 68th percentile of 10-year range, tagged mild-negative. US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.28% yield (latest, up from 5.24% prior) — at 96th percentile, tagged strong-negative, rising 3 of last 5 periods. BOJ rate at 1% p.a. US equity valuations at all-time highs (S&P 500 at 100th percentile) — take profits on US tech longs.","pct_10y":96,"pct_note":"US 10-year yield at 96th percentile is a regime shift signal. Last time yields were this elevated (2023), EM currencies fell 5-8% and equity volatility spiked 30-40%.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening; RBI Intervention Likely Soon","data_text":"INR at 96.15 ₹ (latest, down from 96.3 ₹ prior) — at 91st percentile of 10-year range, tagged strong-negative. Recent trend shows INR at 95.24 → 94.34 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 95.24 → 96.15 over last 6 months — volatile and weakening bias. FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month prior) — at 83rd percentile, but recent trend shows -114 → -3,111.9 → 29,631 (volatile, only 1 of last 2 up). signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter prior) — at 6th percentile of 10-year range, tagged strong-negative. Recent trend shows 13.2 → 5.2 → 13.2 → 21 → 13.2 → 21 (highly volatile, but 3 of last 5 up). Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (latest, down from 15.1% prior) — at 42nd percentile, stable. Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (latest, down from 5% prior) — at 7th percentile, tagged strong-positive, falling 2 of last 5 periods. Nifty IT index flat while office absorption volatile. Rent in Bengaluru at 100.6 ₹/sqft/mo (latest, up from 94 ₹/sqft/mo prior) — at 57th percentile. Rent in Mumbai at 125 ₹/sqft/mo (latest, up from 117.9 ₹/sqft/mo prior) — at 38th percentile.","implication":"Office absorption volatility masks a structural shift: Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses (hence the 21 mn sq ft spikes), while traditional IT services are shrinking footprints. Retail mall vacancy collapse (4.8%, 7th percentile) signals e-commerce saturation and omnichannel retail recovery — this is a consumer strength signal, not a weakness. Overweight retail REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) on omnichannel thesis, not office REITs. Underweight traditional IT services; overweight GCC-exposed IT consulting and software product companies. The office market is NOT a proxy for IT sector health anymore.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is historically a bear signal for IT, but retail vacancy at 7th percentile is a bull signal for consumer. The divergence signals a structural reallocation, not cyclical weakness. Last time office and retail diverged this sharply (2019-20), retail recovered 300 bps while office stayed weak for 3 years.","is_surprise":true}

{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry the Headline — Goods Economy Quietly Decelerates

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is services-driven: PMI Services 54.5 vs PMI Manufacturing 52.8, the widest gap in four months.
  • IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8% YoY; core sector decelerated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — goods-economy momentum is fading.
  • But IIP Capital Goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile) confirm the investment cycle is intact.
  • GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month — up from ₹1,74,116 cr / month — is a 15% single-month jump that warrants decomposition against e-way bill data before treating as a demand breakout.

The tension: The headline composite flatters: services buoyancy is masking goods deceleration, and a GST print of this magnitude in a single month historically reflects advance filings or formalization reclassification as much as genuine demand.

Bottom line: Watch PMI Manufacturing: a print below 52 would confirm goods-economy stall and force a downgrade to the consensus 7.8% YoY growth narrative.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Bond Market Tightening Where Central Banks Won't — EM Pays the Price

The facts:

  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.28% yield (96th percentile) — up from 5.24% — is embedding real tightening that the Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (68th percentile) does not capture.
  • US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR is recovering from 1.5%, but US Core PCE at 3.01% YoY (sticky, up from 2.98%) means the Fed cannot pivot — the bond market is doing the work.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is unwinding the yen carry trade; Euro Stoxx 50 at a 100th-percentile 6,242 and Nikkei at a 100th-percentile 70,147 are priced for a world where this tightening does not transmit.
  • But China GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0%) with PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) removes the commodity-reflation escape valve for EM.

The tension: DM equity indices are at 100th-percentile valuations while the bond market is pricing a tightening cycle that has not ended — and China's demand contraction means commodity prices cannot bail out EM current accounts.

Bottom line: BOJ is the underappreciated tail: each 25bps hike unwinds carry trades that have funded EM positioning — watch the next BOJ meeting for the signal that forces India FII repatriation.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs — But the Funding Gap Underneath Is Widening

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising two consecutive months) and DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile) are providing a structural bid to Indian equities.
  • MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile) and SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile) confirm the retail financialisation trend is deepening.
  • But bank deposit growth at 10.8% YoY vs credit growth at 17.1% YoY — a 630bps divergence — means the same household savings flowing into MFs are not flowing into bank deposits, tightening the system's funding base.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) looks strong but the recent sequence is -₹114 cr → -₹3,112 cr → +₹29,631 cr — one month of recovery after two of outflows, not a trend.

The tension: Record SIP and DII flows are masking a structural deposit shortfall: retail money is choosing mutual funds over bank deposits, which compresses the deposit base precisely as credit demand accelerates.

Bottom line: If deposit growth does not recover toward 13% YoY within two months, expect RBI macro-prudential action — risk-weight hikes on unsecured lending — before any rate move.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand and Premium Supply Diverge From Equity REIT Pricing

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5 percentage points vs prior period), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Premium (₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr) commands 34% of new launch supply and luxury (₹1.5–₹2.5 cr) a further 24% — developers are building for the top half of the market; affordable (14% of launches.
  • Hyderabad leads with sales +15% YoY and launches +120% YoY — a supply surge that, at 29 months of unsold inventory, risks price pressure; NCR sales at -1% YoY despite prices up 12% YoY signals affordability fatigue.
  • But office REITs are pricing the opposite signal: Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit (down from ₹429), Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹498), Brookfield at ₹263/unit (down from ₹330) — all down 14–31% from prior, while Bengaluru office rents rose to ₹100.6/sqft/mo from ₹94.

The tension: Physical office rents are rising and retail mall vacancy is at a 7th-percentile 4.8% vacant — yet listed REITs have de-rated 14–31%, suggesting the market is pricing US 10Y yield competition, not underlying asset fundamentals.

Bottom line: REIT de-rating is a US 10Y yield story, not an India real estate story — if US 10Y stabilises below 5.0% yield, Embassy and Mindspace offer a mean-reversion trade with fundamental support.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — US Yields Sit Behind All of Them

The facts:

  • US 10Y at 5.28% yield (96th percentile, rising 3 of last 5 periods) — every 25bps further compresses India's rate differential, accelerates FII outflows, and pressures INR toward 97–98 ₹.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $100.47/bbl — a $10/bbl spike adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill, widens CAD by ~40bps, and feeds CPI with a two-quarter lag.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY — if deposit growth does not recover, RBI risk-weight action or a liquidity squeeze in NBFC wholesale funding is the next macro-prudential move.
  • Hyderabad residential launches at +120% YoY against 29 months of unsold inventory — a supply-demand mismatch that, if sales momentum reverses, could trigger developer stress in the city leading the national launch cycle.

The tension: All four risks have a common amplifier: a US 10Y yield that stays above 5.25% yield tightens India's external financing, pressures INR, raises import costs, and reduces RBI's room to ease — a feedback loop the base case does not price.

Bottom line: Watch US 10Y Treasury this week: a print above 5.35% yield would force RBI FX intervention, compress domestic liquidity, and make the CD ratio stress acute within 30 days.

"}
